policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere ובתבונתו and ketiv ובתובנתו are orthographic variants of the same noun 'understanding'; ASV 'by his understanding' renders either identically. The note 'Or, stilleth' is alternative_rendering on the verb and does not touch this unit. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

ASV 'the outskirts of his ways' is plural, matching qere דרכיו 'his ways'; ketiv דרכו 'his way' is singular and would have been rendered 'his way'. None of the verse's alternative_rendering notes bears on this word.

ASV 'the thunder of his power' is singular and abstract; that is a normal rendering of ketiv גבורתו 'his might' but also of the abstract plural qere גבורותיו, and the ASV's own note 'Or, mighty deeds' shows the translators treated the word as renderable in the plural. That note is alternative_rendering and cannot decide the unit, so the English number does not settle the reading. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
